memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Then the king of Sodom, the king of Gomorrah... marched out and drew up their battle lines in the Valley of Siddim... Now the Valley of Siddim was full of tar pits, and when the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah fled, some of the men fell into them and the rest fled to the hills. - Gen 14:8-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The battle turns into a rout, and then something almost comic in its tragedy: the fleeing kings fall into tar pits. The very ground they fought over swallowed them. They marched out confident, drew up their lines, and ended up sunk in the muck of their own valley.

There is a picture here worth pausing on. The kings of Sodom and Gomorrah were fighting to hold onto their land - the rich, well-watered plain that Lot had found so attractive. And that land betrayed them. What looked like the prize became the trap.

That is so often the way with the things we chase without God. They promise security and swallow us instead. The career we sacrifice everything for, the relationship we compromise to keep, the wealth we bend our integrity to gain - the ground we fight so hard to stand on can give way beneath us.

Jesus told of a man who built bigger barns to secure his future, only to hear God say, "You fool! This very night your life will be demanded from you" (Luke 12:20). Only one foundation holds. Build "on the rock" (Matt 7:24-25), and when the ground gives way - as it will - you will still be standing.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- What are you standing on that could give way beneath you?
- Is your life built on the rock, or on ground that only looks solid?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord, keep me from building my life on ground that will give way. Be my rock and my sure foundation, so that when everything shifts, I am still standing in You.
Amen.
